story: As a new child player, I want to learn by placing three guided blocks, so that I can start without reading long instructions.
acceptance: Tutorial can be replayed and completed without audio.
implementation: Tutorial: select, preview, confirm three moves; help is replayable.
validation: UI: guided tutorial completes.

story: As a child learning the game, I want to play an untimed beginner board with simpler pieces, so that I can practise without feeling rushed.
acceptance: Difficulty is visibly labelled and results stay outside ranked tables.
implementation: Separate untimed beginner generator; practice is labelled assisted/unranked.
validation: Engine simple-pieces and UI practice tests.

story: As a child who recognises shapes more easily than colours, I want to identify blocks using outlines and patterns, so that I can understand the board without relying on colour.
acceptance: All occupied cells remain distinguishable in every theme.
implementation: Cell symbols + boundaries in pattern/high-contrast mode.
validation: Code and browser inspection; physical vision/colour-blind usability pending.

story: As a child sharing a family device, I want to use a separate local profile, so that my progress does not overwrite my family's.
acceptance: Switching profiles restores the correct progress and settings.
implementation: Profile-scoped saved game, settings, history, stars and records.
validation: Storage round-trip and profile-switch UI checks.

story: As a child player, I want to earn predictable cosmetic stars by solving puzzles, so that I can see my progress without purchases or ads.
acceptance: Rewards never require an ad or provide ranked advantages.
implementation: A completed round with at least three placements earns stars; Garden at five.
validation: Code rules; no payment or ad path required.

story: As a child playing with family, I want to join a guardian-approved private challenge, so that I can play with people my family knows.
acceptance: Child profiles cannot enter public matchmaking or searchable teams.
implementation: Private rooms require guardian approval for child profiles. Revoking approval blocks access to active rooms.
validation: Mobile PIN flow and server invite/revocation tests. Guardian identity and consent verification remain external.

story: As a child player, I want to use preset friendly reactions, so that I can celebrate without exchanging personal details.
acceptance: No free-text chat, photo uploads or direct messages.
implementation: Allowlisted reactions only; no free-text chat, DMs or photo upload.
validation: Preset/rate-limit server tests.

story: As a child who gets stuck, I want to receive a free practice hint, so that I can learn what a useful move looks like.
acceptance: Hints are unavailable in scored competitive attempts.
implementation: Free practice hint; no ranked help/undo control.
validation: Practice UI and ranked-integrity server tests.

story: As a child player, I want to see a clear stopping point after a round, so that I can leave without losing earned rewards.
acceptance: No streak-loss or team-loss warning is shown on exit.
implementation: Finish confirmation is cancellable. Round result and voluntary exit preserve earned progress.
validation: Tutorial/results UI and interaction checks.

story: As a guardian of a child aged 7–12, I want to set play reminders and approve sharing or social access, so that I can manage my child's participation.
acceptance: Reminders work locally; external sharing is gated for child profiles.
implementation: PIN-gated online social and sharing settings and child reminder changes. Current social approval is visible in the profile.
validation: Mobile guardian controls and server revocation checks. Device-level parental enforcement remains open.

story: As a school student, I want to join a private room with a short code, so that I can challenge known friends easily.
acceptance: Expired codes fail clearly and hosts can remove unstarted seats.
implementation: Expiring eight-character room codes and direct invite links. A link survives setup and previews terms before claiming a seat. Hosts can remove a waiting guest.
validation: Browser link, preflight, host removal and same-code rejoin checks. Native link handoff needs device acceptance.

story: As a student competing with friends, I want to receive the same piece sequence and scoring rules, so that the result reflects our decisions.
acceptance: Server replay produces the recorded score for both players.
implementation: One shared versioned seed/shape/scoring engine and authoritative replay.
validation: 500 simulations plus two-client HTTP/UI tests.

story: As a student with homework and limited time, I want to choose a short turn-limited challenge, so that I know roughly how much commitment I am making.
acceptance: Turn allowance and overall expiry are visible before joining.
implementation: The pre-join review provides room type, invitation expiry, match window and placement limit before claiming a seat.
validation: Browser invitation dialog plus server tests that preview is read-only, gated, and respects expiry.

story: As a student on an unstable connection, I want to rejoin a match after a brief drop, so that one network interruption does not immediately end my game.
acceptance: Reconnect within the grace period restores confirmed server state.
implementation: Live reconnect restores authoritative state within the grace period. A successful same-code rejoin clears stale access errors.
validation: Browser reconnect after guest removal plus server grace-period tests.

story: As a student who enjoys improvement, I want to review a completed match's decisive moves, so that I can understand how to play better.
acceptance: Opponent moves are revealed only after both attempts are final.
implementation: Move-by-move post-final replay and largest scoring move jump.
validation: Replay equality and two-client replay UI checks.

story: As a student who enjoys team play, I want to join a private friend team, so that we can compete together.
acceptance: Only approved members occupy roster slots.
implementation: Private team codes, captain-approved requests, three-player cap.
validation: Team membership/roster tests.

story: As a student who dislikes public pressure, I want to keep my results visible only to invited friends, so that I can compete comfortably.
acceptance: Profiles are private by default; no real-name requirement.
implementation: Aliases and authenticated membership checks; private by default.
validation: Outsider access and recovery isolation tests.

story: As a student with limited data, I want to practise offline and submit eligible challenges when connected, so that I can play without a constant connection.
acceptance: Offline practice is clearly unranked; ranked submission needs verification.
implementation: Native offline practice and Solo remain unranked. An opened private async challenge can queue moves and finish offline. The server applies the batch atomically against the confirmed board before the deadline.
validation: Browser disconnect/reload/reconnect check plus atomicity, retry and expiry tests.

story: As a student who wants recognition, I want to earn skill badges for difficult verified achievements, so that my achievements represent ability.
acceptance: Badge rules are visible and cannot be satisfied by ad-earned tools.
implementation: Server-verified badges can be exported as achievement cards with only the sharer's alias. Local badges are labelled separately.
validation: Engine badge checks, league awards and browser PNG export.

story: As a student taking a break, I want to mute competition reminders temporarily, so that the game fits around my priorities.
acceptance: Disabled reminders are not replaced with urgency notifications.
implementation: Per-profile quiet mode and one-hour mute cover break and deadline reminders. The foreground inbox remains available for match results.
validation: A browser test exercised a real upcoming async deadline while muted and after resuming.

story: As a college student, I want to create a private league and invite classmates, so that we have an organised competition.
acceptance: Invites, roster limits and entry deadline are shown.
implementation: Private 4- and 8-team leagues support up to 40 characters in season names. Invitation expiry closes signups. A filled league can still start after that deadline.
validation: Browser late-start and server expiry checks.

story: As a team captain, I want to lock a roster before the season starts, so that fixtures stay fair.
acceptance: Post-lock replacements follow an explicit recorded rule.
implementation: Entering locks three approved players. Completing a season or expiring an underfilled one releases the team lock. Historical rosters retain their players and access rules.
validation: Roster lock, repeat season and archive privacy tests.

story: As a competitive player, I want to see standings with published tie-breakers, so that I understand how qualification works.
acceptance: Equal records resolve by declared rules without hidden changes.
implementation: Club explains fixture points and standings points separately. Head-to-head reapplication, individual wins and explicit deciders determine qualification.
validation: Standings and tied qualification tests.

story: As a league organiser, I want to run qualifiers, an eliminator and a final, so that the season has meaningful progression.
acceptance: Bracket advancement follows stored results and defined seeding.
implementation: Server results advance Qualifier 1, Eliminator, Qualifier 2 and Final. New Championship registration is gated on the server.
validation: Server gate check and full 8-team season from validated moves.

story: As a player proud of a good match, I want to share a spoiler-free result with a replayable challenge link, so that friends can try the same contest.
acceptance: No opponent identity is included without that player's permission.
implementation: Result and verified achievement cards support preview and PNG export with the sharer's alias. Same-seed unranked challenge links survive setup.
validation: Browser PNG, card privacy and first-run challenge checks. Native sharing requires a device.

story: As a player comparing strategies, I want to view side-by-side replays after a match, so that I can learn from the difference in our decisions.
acceptance: Replay works with the original game-rules version.
implementation: Two boards at a shared move index; side-by-side wide, stacked narrow.
validation: Two-client final replay UI; exact shared-engine replay tests.

story: As a busy college student, I want to answer a friend challenge asynchronously, so that we do not need to be online together.
acceptance: Both attempts use the stored sequence and equal rules.
implementation: 24-hour asynchronous private duels, identical sequences and limits.
validation: Async expiry and sequence tests.

story: As an adult who enjoys personalisation, I want to unlock a non-transferable cosmetic preview through an optional ad, so that I can try a style without changing competition.
acceptance: Reward is disclosed, granted once and has no scoring effect.
implementation: Adult-only optional cosmetic offer and idempotent complete/skip/fail lifecycle.
validation: Development provider tests only; no live ad SDK or signed reward verification.

story: As a player who wants fair rankings, I want to enter matches without purchasable boosters or ad advantages, so that winning feels credible.
acceptance: Undo, reroll and revive requests are rejected in ranked rooms.
implementation: Server rejects ranked undo, reroll, revive and booster flags; validates coordinates/sequence.
validation: Integrity, duplicate action and impossible-move tests.

story: As a league participant, I want to report a suspicious result or inappropriate team name, so that our competition stays trustworthy.
acceptance: Reports are rate-limited, recorded and reviewable.
implementation: Rate-limited private reports, durable records and local admin review command.
validation: Reporting tests. No staffed moderation operation is supplied.

story: As an office worker, I want to resume my solo board after an interruption, so that short breaks do not erase progress.
acceptance: Returning restores the last confirmed local move.
implementation: Last confirmed solo state autosaves locally. Storage failures have an inline retry.
validation: Reload/resume browser UI test.

story: As an adult playing in a noisy place, I want to understand all feedback with sound off, so that headphones are unnecessary.
acceptance: Tutorials, errors and results have visual equivalents.
implementation: Play, tutorial, errors, results and connectivity have visible text. Status and error toasts use live-region semantics and explicit dismissal.
validation: Browser gameplay and toast interaction checks.

story: As a busy adult, I want to choose between relaxed play and a fixed-length duel, so that I can match the game to my available time.
acceptance: Time pressure and turn limits are shown before play.
implementation: Solo vs live 30-placement duel vs async 24-hour challenge.
validation: Home/room UI and mode rule tests.

story: As an office-team organiser, I want to set fixture windows rather than exact start times, so that colleagues can participate around work.
acceptance: Attempts expire at a visible server deadline.
implementation: Organiser chooses 1–168-hour fixture windows; deadlines enforced server-side.
validation: League scheduling and clock-based expiry tests.

story: As a parent playing with a child, I want to use pass-and-play on one phone, so that we can enjoy a family challenge together.
acceptance: Turns are separated and local scores are marked unranked.
implementation: Pass-and-play handoff removes the first board and score from the rendered screen and uses an opaque overlay. Player two starts with the same sequence.
validation: Browser handoff privacy, identical initial trays and unranked result checks.

story: As an adult who dislikes intrusive ads, I want to see ads only at clear breaks and decline rewarded offers, so that I remain in control.
acceptance: No ad overlays the board; declining keeps free play available.
implementation: No board ads; test offers have decline/failure states and never block rematches.
validation: Provider simulation tests. Real ad scheduling/delivery is absent.

story: As an adult who prefers uninterrupted play, I want to purchase removal of automatic ads, so that I can choose a quieter experience.
acceptance: Purchase restoration works; optional rewarded ads remain separately labelled.
implementation: The restoration control gives a neutral unavailable-billing notice.
validation: Browser notice test. Store products, receipt verification and sandbox restoration remain open.

story: As a player using a second device, I want to recover my account and earned progress, so that a phone change does not erase my history.
acceptance: Verified sign-in restores cloud records without merging another profile.
implementation: Bearer-key recovery and revision-checked cloud backup; personal vs verified records separated.
validation: Restart/recovery/cloud isolation tests. Not email/phone-verified identity.

story: As a player on a budget phone, I want to disable particles and use simple animations, so that the game remains responsive.
acceptance: Core play is tested on representative budget Android hardware.
implementation: Low-effects setting disables placement/clear/score effects.
validation: Browser execution checked; no representative budget Android hardware benchmark.

story: As an adult monitoring screen time, I want to see my session duration and optional break reminder, so that I can make an informed choice about continuing.
acceptance: Reminder dismissal never removes rewards or penalises a team.
implementation: Duration tracks foreground time. Optional break reminders are nonblocking, saved to the inbox, and respect quiet mode.
validation: Browser timed mute and notification drawer checks.

story: As a player who prefers larger text, I want to increase interface text size, so that labels and scores are comfortable to read.
acceptance: Controls remain usable at supported maximum text size.
implementation: At 200% text, compact screens give the heading its own line and stack the placement actions.
validation: Browser header-height and label-containment checks at 320 px, plus phone-width interaction checks.

story: As a player who wants clearer visuals, I want to use a high-contrast board with patterned blocks, so that occupied cells are easy to distinguish.
acceptance: Board information never depends on hue alone.
implementation: High-contrast board plus automatic symbols and optional normal-theme patterns.
validation: Browser inspection; no accessibility certification claimed.

story: As a player with less precise touch input, I want to tap a piece and then tap its destination, so that dragging is not my only option.
acceptance: Preview, confirm and cancel all work without dragging.
implementation: Tap piece, destination, preview, confirm and cancel. Touch drag uses pointer handling on web and keeps the move as a preview until confirmation.
validation: Mobile Chromium drag and placement tests. Native gesture verification remains open.

story: As a player who prefers unhurried play, I want to choose untimed solo and asynchronous challenges, so that quick reflexes are not required.
acceptance: Live blitz is optional and never the default mode.
implementation: Untimed solo/practice and async attempts; no default blitz.
validation: Mode and async expiry tests.

story: As a new player, I want to replay a plain-language tutorial, so that I can learn at my own pace.
acceptance: Help is accessible from the board without losing solo progress.
implementation: Replayable tutorial and accessible Help dialog without replacing the saved solo board.
validation: Browser keyboard dismissal and board preservation checks.

story: As a player sensitive to visual motion, I want to reduce animation and disable vibration, so that the game feels comfortable.
acceptance: Flashes and celebratory motion are removed in this setting.
implementation: System reduced motion respected, user motion/low-effects toggles, optional vibration off by default.
validation: Browser settings; OS/native assistive behaviour pending.

story: As a grandparent or older relative, I want to join a private family league, so that I can connect with relatives across age groups.
acceptance: Only invited accounts appear in the league.
implementation: Invited, guardian-approved family members can join a private league. An outsider cannot see it, and revoking approval blocks active fixture access.
validation: Server family-league integration and mobile Club walk-through. Production guardian verification remains open.

story: As a player who enjoys personal goals, I want to track my own improvement without a public rank, so that progress feels rewarding at my level.
acceptance: Personal, assisted and verified competitive records are separated.
implementation: Local personal/assisted/authoritative competitive bests separated; private history.
validation: Cloud record separation tests and profile screen.

story: As a player who prefers Hindi or Marathi, I want to read menus and help in my preferred language, so that language does not prevent participation.
acceptance: Translated text and Devanagari fonts fit supported layouts.
implementation: Hindi and Marathi include core menus, tutorial, move counts, line clears, fit cues, board accessibility labels and several match and league statuses.
validation: Browser selected-text checks and Devanagari layout inspection. Secondary strings and native-speaker review remain open.

story: As a player who values simplicity, I want to use a home screen with a few clear choices, so that I can find play, friends and help easily.
acceptance: Primary play is reachable in one tap after setup.
implementation: Primary Solo/Resume one tap after setup; Friends/Club/You secondary.
validation: Onboarding and one-tap Play UI test.
